1	# WP-007 — Unit Tests: Custom Variables and Config Partials
     2	
     3	## Description
     4	
     5	Add unit tests for the custom variables merge order in `buildContext()` and the config-level partials injection in `buildSuite()`. These tests verify that the wiring from WP-002 (Custom Variables) and WP-004 (Config Partials) produces the correct merge behaviour.
     6	
     7	## Scope — Files to Modify
     8	
     9	- `tests/builders/` — new or extended test file(s) for variables merge and partials merge verification
    10	
    11	## Dependencies
    12	
    13	- WP-002 (Custom Variables Wiring — the variables merge being tested)
    14	- WP-004 (Config Partials and onPartials Hook Wiring — the partials merge being tested)
    15	
    16	## Active Pipeline Stages
    17	
    18	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    19	
    20	## Acceptance Criteria
    21	
    22	1. A test confirms `BuildConfig.variables` values appear in the rendered context when no higher-priority source provides them
    23	2. A test confirms `SuiteConfig.variables` values override `BuildConfig.variables` values for the same key
    24	3. A test confirms persona YAML values override both `SuiteConfig.variables` and `BuildConfig.variables`
    25	4. A test confirms `_shared.yaml` values override `BuildConfig.variables` (but are overridden by persona YAML)
    26	5. A test confirms `BuildConfig.partials` entries are present in the rendered template output
    27	6. A test confirms file-based partials with the same stem name override `BuildConfig.partials`
    28	7. All new tests pass
    29	8. All existing tests continue to pass
    30	
    31	## Notes
    32	
    33	- Some tests may need to use the full `buildPersona()` or `buildSuite()` functions with fixture suites to verify end-to-end merge behaviour.
    34	- Alternatively, if `buildContext()` is exported or testable via its callers, unit-level tests can verify merge order directly.
    35	- Check whether the test fixtures in `fixtures/sample-suite/` are sufficient or need small additions.
    36	- Estimated complexity: Medium.

   512	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   513	// buildSuite — all personas in one suite × one target
   514	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   515	
   516	/**
   517	 * Build all personas in a suite for a single output target.
   518	 *
   519	 * Pipeline:
   520	 *   1. Load `_shared.yaml` for the suite
   521	 *   2. Load merged partials (config.partials → shared → suite-local)
   522	 *   3. Run `onSuiteInit` on all plugins
   523	 *   3a. Run `onPartials` on all plugins (highest priority: may override any file-based partial)
   524	 *   4. Discover all persona YAML files
   525	 *   5. Call `buildPersona()` for each
   526	 *
   527	 * @param suiteName    Identifier for this suite
   528	 * @param suiteConfig  Suite configuration
   529	 * @param config       Top-level BuildConfig
   530	 * @param plugins      Registered plugins
   531	 * @param target       Target output format
   532	 * @param agentMap     Pre-built cross-suite agent name map
   533	 * @param registry     Target registry to use. Defaults to `defaultRegistry`.
   534	 *   **Two-registry limitation:** If you pass a custom `TargetRegistry` only
   535	 *   to `build()` (via `config.targetRegistry`) and call `buildSuite()`
   536	 *   directly without also passing that registry here, your custom targets
   537	 *   will not be visible — `defaultRegistry` will be used instead. Either
   538	 *   pass the same registry instance explicitly, or call `build()` to have
   539	 *   the registry forwarded automatically.
   540	 * @returns            Array of BuildResult objects, one per persona
   541	 */
   542	export async function buildSuite(
   543	  suiteName: string,
   544	  suiteConfig: SuiteConfig,
   545	  config: BuildConfig,
   546	  plugins: PersonaBuildPlugin[],
   547	  target: string,
   548	  agentMap: Record<string, string> = {},
   549	  registry: TargetRegistry = defaultRegistry,
   550	): Promise<BuildResult[]> {
   551	  // ── 1. Load shared metadata ───────────────────────────────────────────────
   552	  const metaSubdir = suiteConfig.metaSubdir ?? 'meta';
   553	  const sharedYamlPath = path.join(suiteConfig.srcDir, metaSubdir, '_shared.yaml');
   554	  const sharedMeta = await loadRawYaml(sharedYamlPath);
   555	
   556	  // ── 2. Load partials (three-layer: config.partials → shared → suite-local) ─
   557	  // Start with config.partials as the lowest-priority base layer.
   558	  let partialsMap: Record<string, string> = { ...(config.partials ?? {}) };
   559	
   560	  if (config.sharedPartialsDir && existsSync(config.sharedPartialsDir)) {
   561	    partialsMap = { ...partialsMap, ...(await loadPartials(config.sharedPartialsDir)) };
   562	  }
   563	
   564	  const partialsSubdir = suiteConfig.partialsSubdir ?? 'partials';
   565	  const suitePartialsDir = path.join(suiteConfig.srcDir, partialsSubdir);
   566	  if (existsSync(suitePartialsDir)) {
   567	    partialsMap = { ...partialsMap, ...(await loadPartials(suitePartialsDir)) };
   568	  }
   569	
   570	  // ── 3. Plugin onSuiteInit ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
   571	  runSuiteInit(plugins, suiteConfig, sharedMeta);
   572	
   573	  // ── 3a. Plugin onPartials ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
   574	  // Invoked after onSuiteInit and after all file-based partials are loaded.
   575	  // Plugins may inject new partials or override any file-based entry.
   576	  partialsMap = runPartials(plugins, partialsMap, suiteName, suiteConfig);
   577	
   578	  // ── 4. Discover persona YAML files ────────────────────────────────────────
   579	  const personaYamlPaths = await discoverSuitePersonaYamls(suiteConfig);
   580	
   581	  // ── 5. Build each persona ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
   582	  const results: BuildResult[] = [];
   583	  for (const yamlPath of personaYamlPaths) {
   584	    const result = await buildPersona(
   585	      yamlPath,
   586	      suiteName,
   587	      suiteConfig,
   588	      sharedMeta,
   589	      partialsMap,
   590	      config,
   591	      plugins,
   592	      target,
   593	      agentMap,
   594	      registry,
   595	    );
   596	    results.push(result);
   597	  }
   598	
   599	  return results;
   600	}
   601	
   602	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   603	// build — top-level entry point
   604	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   605	
   606	/**
   607	 * Top-level build orchestrator.
   608	 *
   609	 * Iterates all `config.suites × config.targets` combinations, calls
   610	 * `buildSuite()` for each, and aggregates the results into a `BuildSummary`.
   611	 *
   612	 * Modes:
   613	 *   - Normal: renders and writes all personas.
   614	 *   - `check: true`: renders without writing; useful for CI staleness checks.
   615	 *   - `strict: true`: throws when any ValidationResult has severity `'error'`
   616	 *     or `'warning'`. All suites are processed before the throw, so output
   617	 *     files **will** be written to disk even when the build ultimately fails.
   618	 *     **For CI usage, combine `strict: true` with `check: true`** to avoid
   619	 *     leaving partial artefacts on disk when validation fails.
   620	 *
   621	 * @param config  Typed build configuration
   622	 * @returns       Aggregated BuildSummary
   623	 * @throws        `Error` when `strict: true` and validation failures exist
   624	 */
   625	export async function build(config: BuildConfig): Promise<BuildSummary> {
   626	  const plugins = config.plugins ?? [];
   627	  const registry = config.targetRegistry ?? defaultRegistry;
   628	  // When a custom registry is supplied and targets are not explicit, build all
   629	  // registered targets. When using the default registry without an explicit
   630	  // targets list, build only targets with defaultEnabled !== false. This
   631	  // preserves the historical two-target default (vscode + claude-code) for
   632	  // existing suite configs that do not configure deep-agents output.
   633	  const targets = config.targets ?? registry.names().filter(n => registry.get(n).defaultEnabled !== false);
   634	  const allResults: BuildResult[] = [];
   635	
   636	  // Pre-scan: build cross-suite agent name map
   637	  const agentMap = await buildAgentNameMap(config);
   638	
   639	  for (const [suiteName, suiteConfig] of Object.entries(config.suites)) {
   640	    for (const target of targets) {
   641	      const suiteResults = await buildSuite(suiteName, suiteConfig, config, plugins, target, agentMap, registry);
   642	      allResults.push(...suiteResults);
   643	    }
   644	  }
   645	
   646	  // Collect strict failures (error + warning severity)
   647	  const strictFailures: ValidationResult[] = config.strict
   648	    ? allResults.flatMap((r) =>
   649	        r.validationResults.filter(
   650	          (v) => v.severity === 'error' || v.severity === 'warning',
   651	        ),
   652	      )
   653	    : [];
   654	
   655	  const success = !config.strict || strictFailures.length === 0;
   656	
   657	  const summary: BuildSummary = {
   658	    success,
   659	    results: allResults,
   660	    strictFailures,
   661	    totalBuilt: allResults.length,
   662	    totalWritten: allResults.filter((r) => r.written).length,
   663	  };
   664	
   665	  if (config.strict && !success) {
   666	    const messages = strictFailures.map((f) => `[${f.severity}] ${f.message}`).join('\n');
   667	    throw new Error(
   668	      `Build failed in strict mode — ${strictFailures.length} validation issue(s):\n${messages}`,
   669	    );
   670	  }
   671	
   672	  return summary;
   673	}
